global: Running from the field again, {player}? Some things never change on this server.
I remember when the first war still had people standing their ground. Those days seem gone.
Retreat is a fine tactic, as long as you don't call it a victory afterward.
Half the veterans here have turned tail once or twice. Doesn't make it any less noticeable.
Ran off before the first clash. Bold of you to leave your own troops to hold the line.
Nobody's counting the scattered riders, but the ones who stayed will remember who left them.
Fast legs, I'll grant that. Shame the banners didn't keep up.
Quite the disappearing act. Try not to lose the road home too.
Some of us came to fight. Others came to watch the dust settle. Makes the record easy to read.
Cut and run before contact. The old hands in this chat have seen that before, and they remember it.
whisper: {player}, a retreat before the line even formed is not a plan. Think about what your riders saw.
I won't pretend that was a fight. You left the field before the first arrow flew.
You want my advice? Stop running and pick a battle you can actually finish.
Chasing you across the map would waste my afternoon. Consider yourself lucky, for now.
That was a sorry exit, {player}. Your company deserved a better captain than that.
Next time you turn tail, at least leave the banners behind. They were never yours to carry off.
I've seen better courage in a sheep pen. Keep your scouts closer next time.
No hard feelings, but I'd rethink the next engagement before your horses get tired.
Running is an honest choice. Just don't expect the same courtesy from the men who stayed.
You scattered the moment the drums started. Work on your nerve before you try the next border.

global: Saw {player}'s party break off before the clash. Could be wisdom, could be bad timing.
Fighting withdrawals are underrated. Plenty of good captains have used one.
Tactical retreat or a rout? The map will tell us in a day or two.
Ran from the field today. Whatever the reason, nobody here needs the details.
Some folks charge in, some fall back. Both have their place when the terrain is wrong.
Keep an eye on {player}'s riders. Nothing wrong with withdrawing early, but it's worth noting.
I've retreated before a bad fight myself, back when this server was younger. Lived to tell it.
The fens are no place to make a stand with a tired company. Sensible move, I suppose.
No judgment yet. Let's see if the retreat was wise or just lucky.
A scattered line means a long night of regrouping. Hope the troops are fed.
whisper: {player}, I saw your party break off before the clash. Was it the terrain or the numbers?
Pulling back is no shame if you live to fight another day. Just don't make it a habit.
Your riders looked spread thin out there. Pick a place to regroup where the ground favors you.
If the enemy was too strong, a retreat was wise. If not, you'll want to figure out why.
Retreating from a fight tells the whole server a little about you. Make sure it says what you intend.
Good call getting out before the lines met, provided your scouts were right about the numbers.
Regroup and rest your horses. Nobody's chasing you tonight, as far as I can tell.
I'd like to hear what you saw before you turned around. Two heads are better than one on the road.
Withdrawing is a skill, {player}. Most people only learn it after they lose a company.
Stay clear of the river crossings for a while. Scouts reported trouble moving in that direction.

global: Good call pulling back, {player}. Living to fight another day beats a bad trade every time.
{player} knows when the odds are wrong. Wise captain, and the server needs more of those.
Smart withdrawal today. Your people will thank you for not feeding them to the lines.
Falling back from that field was the right move. Plenty of veterans would have stayed and lost the lot.
Retreat with your banners held high is still a retreat worth respect. Well done, {player}.
Some would call that cowardice. I call it keeping your troops alive. Good judgment.
I've made that same retreat more than once. Never regretted it, and neither should {player}.
Tactical withdrawal, clean and quick. Exactly what the new folks should learn from watching.
Nobody lost a company today thanks to {player}'s sense. Keep that instinct sharp.
Quick feet and a clear head saved a lot of trouble out there. Nicely handled.
whisper: {player}, that was a sensible withdrawal. The field was not yours to win today, and you knew it.
You kept your riders intact, which is more than most would manage in that spot. Well judged.
Don't let anyone shame you for falling back. Your troops will be fighting again next week because of it.
I was watching from the ridge. That retreat was clean, and the men were in good order.
Pull back, rest, and restock. Once your company's fed, the next fight will go much better for you.
Good instincts today, {player}. The line you avoided would have cost you a lot of good men.
Take the lesson from this one. Knowing when to leave is as valuable as knowing when to charge.
Lost ground is easy to earn back. Your company is the thing that matters, and you kept it whole.
If you want a second opinion on the map before the next move, I'm happy to look it over with you.
That was a proper retreat, {player}. Keep your banners up and your wits about you on the road.
